parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is declared presentation because of the **/*.module.ts pattern. For a Nest module, that role means wiring: imports, controllers and providers. Choosing the persistence module from database config and registering the controller and service fit that role. But inside the MulterModule.registerAsync useFactory, the file also implements the local file-storage adapter inline: diskStorage with a hard-coded './files' destination and its own filename generation (random string plus the lower-cased original extension). That is filesystem persistence, which belongs to the infrastructure kind; the folder path src/files/infrastructure/uploader/local also points there. The fileFilter also hard-codes an upload policy, a jpg/jpeg/png/gif allowlist with its own error payload. That rule belongs to an application service or validation component, not module wiring. This is borderline, because Nest modules often act as composition roots and type checks at the HTTP boundary can be read as transport validation. That lowers confidence.

violations.message: The MulterModule.registerAsync useFactory sets up local filesystem storage inline: diskStorage with destination './files' and a custom filename generator using randomStringGenerator plus the original extension. That is infrastructure (storage adapter) logic inside a module declared as presentation.

The fileFilter in useFactory hard-codes the allowed upload types (jpg/jpeg/png/gif) and the cantUploadFileType rejection. That policy belongs to an application or validation component, not presentation module wiring.
